doc.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1978-Fall Transcript

title: Racial barriers and rough Chalmette audiences
summary: He says he never had racial trouble with mixed groups until the 1970s in Chalmette.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: When you first started playing, and I guess through the early 60s, were there a lot of racial barriers?
I never was bothered with it myself. I mean I've been playing with mixed groups and mixed houses all my life. I was raised up with white people to tell you the truth of them.
So New Orleans has always been better than I guess some areas in that respect.
Yeah, I've never had any trouble with races. Only here lately, since the 70s when I started going down in Chalamet part of town. Those people don't like nobody.
We go after Chalamet. They're kind of rough down there. They're pretty rough on us when we don't play their requests.
